WMT.rationale: Walmart's franchise quality is high: dominant U.S. grocery position (~21% share), successful layering of high-margin digital revenue streams (advertising +37% YoY, membership +17.4%, eCommerce +26%), and disciplined capital return ($50B combined buyback authorization). Q1 FY2027 showed solid YoY earnings growth (+19.6% EPS) on +7.3% revenue growth, with operating margin expanding to 4.2% and ROE improving to 23%. However, the stock is not cheap: trailing PE of 41.7x yields only 2.4% — roughly 205bp below the 10-year Treasury — and demands continued double-digit earnings growth. The recent de-rating from ~54x to ~42x is directionally positive but merely brings valuation to the lower end of a still-elevated range (38.9x–55.4x). Near-term headwinds are real: fuel costs cut ~$175M from Q1 operating income, regulatory pharmacy pressures knocked ~100bp off U.S. comps, consumer stress at the low end is mounting, and FCF is declining as capex peaks at ~3.5% of sales. The mix-shift thesis is credible but early — consolidated margin gains remain modest at 4.2% operating margin. Net assessment: a durable, evolving franchise with identifiable margin-expansion levers, but priced for smooth execution with limited margin of safety. Mildly attractive on balance, with the recent pullback and near-term guidance raise (6-8% OI growth) providing a modest positive tilt.
key_factors: Q1 FY2027 revenue $177.75B, +7.3% YoY; EPS diluted $0.67 vs $0.56, +19.6% YoY; operating income $7.49B, +5.0% YoY
Trailing PE 41.7x near bottom of 12-month range (38.9x–55.4x) after de-rating from ~54x in May 2026, but 2.4% earnings yield still well below 10Y Treasury at 4.45%
High-margin digital revenue scaling: advertising ~$6.4B run rate growing 37% YoY, membership fee revenue +17.4% (28.4M members), eCommerce +26%
Operating margin 4.2%, net margin 3.2%, ROE 23.0% — all improving YoY but thin and vulnerable to cost headwinds
Fuel costs cut ~$175M from Q1 operating income (~250bp headwind); regulatory pharmacy pressures knocked ~100bp off U.S. comps
Management raised FY guidance: constant-currency sales growth 3.5-4.5% (upper end), operating income growth 6-8%; Q2 adjusted EPS guided $0.72-$0.74
FCF declining per analyst estimates (FY2026 ~$14.9B to FY2027E ~$11.3B) as capex peaks at ~3.5% of sales for supply-chain automation
$50B combined buyback authorization ($30B active + $20B supplemental) and 53 consecutive years of dividend increases signal capital discipline
Consumer stress at lower-income end flagged by management; trade-down from higher-income households ($100K+ driving ~75% of share gains) could reverse
Class action lawsuit filed in Massachusetts (2026-06-06) alleging unlawful hiring practices — potential incremental compliance costs on thin margins
